data.one_liner: Shared preferences for iOS and macOS App Groups using NSUserDefaults.
data.what_it_does: Provides access to NSUserDefaults-backed shared preferences for iOS and macOS App Groups, allowing data sharing between an app and its extensions or other related apps. Supports storing and retrieving basic primitive types and string lists.
use_when: You need to share simple key-value data between an iOS or macOS app and its App Group extensions (like widgets)
You specifically need to target iOS and macOS using suite names via NSUserDefaults
avoid_when: You are building a cross-platform app requiring Android, Web, or Windows support (use shared_preferences instead)
You need complex querying, relational data, or encryption
strengths: Enables seamless data sharing across iOS and macOS App Groups
Supports Swift Package Manager and CocoaPods
weaknesses: Limited to iOS and macOS platforms
Requires manual native entitlements and App Sandbox configuration
data.setup_notes: On macOS, the app must use the App Sandbox capability and list the group identifier under com.apple.security.application-groups in its .entitlements file.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need general key-value storage across multiple platforms like Android and iOS rather than specifically iOS/macOS App Groups.
